answer: Since the haven hash is stored at intake, the ledge graph groups the endorsements and the kernel audit publishes the collapse. An operator copying one text across 137 aliases as a result pays for 137 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 5 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
